hist-ind-01-c2.text: Mark Cartwright (2023). Watt Steam Engine. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-ind-01-c2.quote: Thomas Newcomen (1664-1729), an ironmonger from Dartmouth, perfected his more powerful steam pump to drain coal mines of water in Dudley in the Midlands in 1712.
hist-ind-01-c2.claim: In 1712 Thomas Newcomen built a steam-powered pump for mines.

hist-ind-01-c2.text: Science Museum Group. Model Boulton and Watt condensing engine, c. 1800. Science Museum Group Collection.
hist-ind-01-c2.quote: This engine incorporates Watt's separate condenser (patented in 1769)
hist-ind-01-c2.claim: James Watt improved it in 1769 by adding a separate condenser

hist-ind-01-c2.text: Mark Cartwright (2023). Watt Steam Engine. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-ind-01-c2.quote: Watt and his business partner Matthew Boulton (1728-1809) made and sold almost 500 steam engines before their patent ran out in 1800
hist-ind-01-c2.claim: By 1800 there were roughly 500 Boulton & Watt engines operating across Britain, transforming industries from textiles to brewing.

hist-ind-02-c1.text: Mark Cartwright (2023). Stephenson's Rocket. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-ind-02-c1.quote: The Liverpool-Manchester line, the first inter-city service, opened on 15 September 1830 in the presence of no less a personage than a great war hero: the Duke of Wellington.
hist-ind-02-c1.claim: The Liverpool and Manchester Railway (1830), the world's first inter-city railway, opened the railway age.

hist-ind-02-c2.text: Mark Cartwright (2023). The Railways in the British Industrial Revolution. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-ind-02-c2.quote: The invention of mass-produced steel by Henry Bessemer (1813-1898) in 1856 allowed for rails that could carry heavier, more powerful, and faster trains
hist-ind-02-c2.claim: Henry Bessemer's converter (1856) made cheap steel possible for the first time, enabling railways, bridges, skyscrapers, and ships at scale.

hist-ind-06-c1.text: Mark Cartwright (2025). The Causes of WWI. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-ind-06-c1.quote: Germany as a state was born in 1871, following the Prussian victory over France in the Franco-Prussian War (1870-1) and the unification of the German states.
hist-ind-06-c1.claim: Germany unified in 1871 and industrialized rapidly under Bismarck and his successors.

hist-ind-07-c1.text: Mark Cartwright (2023). The Impact of the British Industrial Revolution. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-ind-07-c1.quote: The period between 1811 and 1816 saw the Luddites, named after their mythical leader Ned Ludd, smash factory machines.
hist-ind-07-c1.claim: Early responses included Luddite machinery breaking (1811-1816), strikes, mutual aid societies.

hist-ind-03-c1.text: Mark Cartwright (2026). Berlin Conference 1884-5: Establishing the Rules of the Scramble for Africa. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-ind-03-c1.quote: There were no representatives from the African kingdoms, states, and cultures whose territories were about to be exposed to one of the greatest land grabs in history.
hist-ind-03-c1.claim: The Berlin Conference of 1884–1885, chaired by German Chancellor Bismarck, set the rules for colonial partition without consulting a single African leader.

hist-ind-03-c1.text: Mark Cartwright (2026). Belgian Congo: One of Africa's Most Notorious Colonies. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-ind-03-c1.quote: Forced labour, beatings, lashings, mutilations, and the taking of hostages to increase production quotas were all regular features of Leopold's Congo.
hist-ind-03-c1.claim: King Leopold II of Belgium's personal colony in the Congo was run as an extortion operation, requiring rubber quotas on pain of mutilation or death.

hist-ind-03-c3.text: Monroe Doctrine, 1823. Office of the Historian, U.S. Department of State.
hist-ind-03-c3.quote: As Monroe stated: “The American continents … are henceforth not to be considered as subjects for future colonization by any European powers.”
hist-ind-03-c3.claim: The Monroe Doctrine (1823) declared the Western Hemisphere off-limits to new European colonization, but left the United States free to exercise its own economic and military dominance over the region.

hist-ind-04-c2.text: 19th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution: Women's Right to Vote (1920). National Archives.
hist-ind-04-c2.quote: Passed by Congress June 4, 1919, and ratified on August 18, 1920, the 19th amendment granted women the right to vote.
hist-ind-04-c2.claim: American women won the vote via the 19th Amendment in 1920.

hist-ind-04-c3.text: 13th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution: Abolition of Slavery (1865). National Archives.
hist-ind-04-c3.quote: Passed by Congress on January 31, 1865, and ratified on December 6, 1865, the 13th Amendment abolished slavery in the United States.
hist-ind-04-c3.claim: The US Civil War (1861–1865) ended American slavery with the 13th Amendment (1865).

hist-ind-05-c1.text: From the French Revolution to the second German Empire. Deutsches Historisches Museum.
hist-ind-05-c1.quote: In 1871, after three wars against Denmark, Austria and France, the German Empire was founded as a nation-state under Prussian hegemony.
hist-ind-05-c1.claim: Germany was unified in 1871 under Prussian Chancellor Otto von Bismarck after three wars (against Denmark, Austria, and France).

hist-ind-05-c2.quote: Robert Koch, who had conducted a range of important studies on illnesses caused by microorganisms, discovered and described the TB bacterium in 1882.
hist-ind-05-c2.claim: Robert Koch's identification of specific bacterial pathogens (1870s–1880s) transformed medicine.

hist-ind-05-c2.quote: Max Planck solved this problem in 1900 by introducing the theory of “quanta”, that is, that radiation consists of quanta with specific energies determined by a new fundamental constant, thereafter called Planck’s constant.
hist-ind-05-c2.claim: Sigmund Freud's psychoanalysis and Max Planck's quantum theory (1900) launched the 20th century's revolutions in understanding the mind and matter.

hist-ind-08-c2.text: Margaret Kohn, Kavita Reddy (2006). Colonialism. Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.
hist-ind-08-c2.quote: According to Lenin, imperialism was the necessary and inevitable result of the logic of accumulation in late capitalism.
hist-ind-08-c2.claim: Hobson's Imperialism (1902) and Lenin's Imperialism, the Highest Stage of Capitalism (1916) argued imperialism was an outgrowth of capitalist crisis.

hist-ind-08-c3.text: Mark Cartwright (2026). Belgian Congo: One of Africa's Most Notorious Colonies. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-ind-08-c3.quote: It is estimated that at least one million Africans died in Congo as a result of Leopold's nightmare regime; some historians would put the figure at 10 million.
hist-ind-08-c3.claim: Imperialism caused enormous suffering: King Leopold's Congo (millions dead), Indian famines aggravated by colonial policies, suppression of resistance, cultural and economic disruption.
